svg.text: Extending Matrix beyond chat: what fits best where
Each cell ranks the solutions for one case, best first.
Highlighted: options built on Iframe + Widget API.
Each user decides what they see; other room members may see
something different or nothing at all.
Same experience for anyone in one Matrix room
Note: the room (state + events) is the only primitive that guarantees
that every member sees the same thing.
A calendar overview spanning all events in all rooms.
A shared document: HedgeDoc with Matrix as the data backend.
a room for a client feature is a hack
Shared management of an external resource (Jira, GitHub) with
interactions: close a ticket, reply in the app, ...
native; the backend is needed anyhow
For one user: build it into the client
A native client implementation or a module for a specific client gives the deepest,
most coherent integration. A widget is not really needed here: a feature for a
single user does not have to look the same across clients.
For a room: Iframe + Widget API
It covers every use case, every member runs the same app in every client, and it
works today. One Widget API implementation per client serves all room features, with
web view on the Widget API (iframe)
A feature specified in a Matrix spec and built into each client natively. The most integrated and coherent result, but
every feature needs a spec and an implementation in every client.
A native extension of one client (Element Web module API, Robrix mini apps). Full UI and client access, but only for
users of that client, so never a guaranteed shared view.
A web app that talks to the Matrix client over a standardised postMessage API, without access to the client-server API
or encryption keys. For one shared room experience, one member picks the app and everyone runs it locally. Use with
caution: "I run JS on my machine that someone else in the room has chosen."
The UI is described in JSON building blocks (A2UI, extensible events) and rendered natively by the client. The logic
runs as a sandboxed wasm process inside the client (a background widget) that talks to the client over the Widget API.
third-party JS with full client access
A widget that is not bound to one room (cross-room, per space, whole client), shown as an iframe or as an A2UI
surface. Written once for every client, but every client has to support the interface.
A bot in the room posts A2UI messages and handles the interactions (relations to the A2UI event, visible to the whole
room). Logic and secrets stay on the server.
A bot keeps the logic and the external connection; a room widget shows its UI. Works today with any UX, but looks less
native. In a DM with the bot (Bot DM) it serves a single user.
Classic bot or appservice: text, commands, reactions, notices (e.g. Hookshot). Works in every client today; the UI is
limited to what the timeline can show.
